texts.facts: Despite repeated requests by the plaintiff, the defendant failed to clear outstanding rent and did not pay a single penny to plaintiff towards arrears of rent, GST and water charges. 5.
texts.arguments: Aggrieved by the acts of the defendant, plaintiff has filed the present suit praying: (i) firstly, for decree of possession of the suit property. Although it is claimed that suit is barred by the provisions of Order VI Rule 15 CPC and also U/o VII Rule 11(a, b, c, d) of CPC as well as Section 6 and 12 of Commercial Courts Act, the said pleas have not been substantiated by cogent averments. The plaintiff intentionally and deliberately with malafide intention and ulterior motive got mentioned period of lease from 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020 instead of 01.10.2019 to 01.09.2024 thereby cheating the defendant and playing fraud upon him. The suit property was let out for five years with provision of extension of lease period with the consent of the parties. The plaintiff was to cooperate with defendant in getting NOCs/license etc. for running Harihar Bhojnalaya. The plaintiff, however, failed to keep his word due to which defendant was unable to run business of bhojnalaya. The plaintiff caused wrongful loss to defendant by failing to give adjustment in the rent due and payable by defendant and rather demanded cash payment towards rent and in this manner he collected monthly rent of Rs.50,000/- per month in cash from defendant. He has alleged that despite repeated requests plaintiff failed to convert the suit property which was a residential property into commercial property and to execute registered agreement to enable him to take NOC/certificate from police, Fire department and MCD due to which defendant was unable to run his business in the name and style of Harihar Bhojnalaya. He is merely doing work of food packing from the suit property as there is no place available for sitting of customers or any kind of commercial activity. 54. The counsel for plaintiff has relied upon judgment in Kamaljeet Singh Vs. Sarabjit Singh, Civil Appeal No.8410/2014 decided on 02.09.2014 by Hon'ble Supreme Court, wherein it has been held as under:- "19. The technical ground raised by counsel for defendant that the lease deed Ex.PW1/2 finds "Description of Document' as mentioned as 'Article 35(ii) Lease with security upto 5 years' and recital in column "Deed Name" as 'Lease with Security upto 5 years' is not sustainable. It is the actual recitals in the lease deed Ex.PW1/2 which are to be considered while drawing conclusion regarding the intent of the parties and thus the fact that period of lease is mentioned as 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020 in the lease deed Ex.PW1/2 is very relevant and it is not possible to give any other interpretation to clause pertaining to period of lease by any stretch of imagination. Jahawar Lal Vohra Through Poa Rajesh ... vs Rajiv Kumar on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10543617/ 12 56. Moreover, contrary to assertion of defendant that there was a provision of renewal of the lease in lease deed, no such term or clause is reflected from Ex.PW1/2.
